title: AI Agent Memory: Running Summary vs Memory Graph — Why Your Chatbot Ships to the Old Address #shorts
caption:
ENGINEERING · AI agent memory: running summary vs memory graph

How do you design a delivery chatbot that doesn't ship to the old address? Summarising the chat isn't the answer.

At turn 5 the customer says Pune. At turn 40, Chennai. To save tokens, your agent drops old messages every 10 turns and rewrites a summary. Four rewrites later, both cities are in it and nothing says which one is newer. The gate timing was gone after the first rewrite.

A summary decides what matters before anyone asks. A memory graph lets the question decide, but only if every fact lands on the same key.

3 rules for AI agent memory:

1. Keep the raw turns. The summary only points into them. For a delivery chat, that's turns 5 and 40.
2. Store every fact as entity, property, value and a timestamp. The newest value on a key wins. For this order, deliver_to = Chennai.
3. Fix the property names before the first write and reject the rest. For this order, deliver_to, never shipping_city.

What isn't a fact ("refund waiting on a photo") stays in a short summary next to the graph.

Save this for your next agent design review. Send it to whoever owns your chatbot's memory.

Blueprint is in the open vault. Link in bio.
